title: Beyond Bilingual: Studying Quadrilingual Code-Switching with Conversational AI
abstract: arXiv:2611.21394v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multilingual speakers choose languages by topic and conversation partner. Large language models (LLMs) support these languages unequally. Research on code-switching with conversational AI has mostly examined bilingual pairs of well-resourced languages. In Cura\c{c}ao and Aruba, many people use Dutch, English, Spanish, and the low-resource Creole Papiamentu/o. In a preregistered study, 42 university students held two five-minute chatbot conversations, one about university life and one about local food and culture. Surveys assessed language background, AI use, and switching comfort. 20 international students in Cura\c{c}ao formed a comparison sample. Participants switched between turns and rarely mixed languages within a message. English dominated both conversations. Participants switched more often in the cultural conversation, where Papiamentu/o and Spanish rose from 15% to 24% of messages. Self-reports showed no lower comfort switchin

translated_title: 超越双语：与会话式AI进行四语码转换的研究
translated_abstract: 多语言使用者会根据话题和对话伙伴来选择语言，而大型语言模型（LLM）对这些语言的支持程度并不均衡。关于会话式AI码转换的研究大多集中在资源丰富的双语语言对上。在库拉索和阿鲁巴，许多人使用荷兰语、英语、西班牙语以及低资源的克里奥尔语——帕皮阿门托语。在一项预注册研究中，42名大学生与聊天机器人进行了两次五分钟的对话，一次关于大学生活，一次关于当地食物和文化。通过问卷调查评估了参与者的语言背景、AI使用情况以及语言转换的舒适度。库拉索的20名国际学生构成了对照样本。参与者在对话轮次之间进行语言切换，很少在单条消息内混用语言。英语在两次对话中均占主导地位。参与者在文化话题的对话中更频繁地切换语言，其中帕皮阿门托语和西班牙语从消息占比的15%上升到24%。自我报告显示参与者的语言转换舒适度并未降低……
tldr: 该研究首次探讨了四语环境（荷兰语、英语、西班牙语与低资源克里奥尔语帕皮阿门托语）下用户与聊天机器人的码转换行为，发现英语虽占主导，但在文化相关话题中低资源语言的使用显著提升，且用户切换语言并无不适感。
en_tdlr: This study offers the first examination of quadrilingual code-switching with conversational AI in Curaçao and Aruba, revealing that English dominates chatbot conversations, but users shift more toward low-resource Papiamentu/o and Spanish when discussing culturally relevant topics without reduced switching comfort.
